transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, I'm Martin. I keep swinging between eating way too much and then trying to "make up for it" with these harsh rules and routines, and it’s starting to take over my days. This pattern started after I recently cut back my hours at work, and my primary doctor urged me to speak with a professional about it.
When you eat way too much, do you feel out of control during those episodes, and do you then do things like vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain?

Yes, once I start eating, it feels like I'm on autopilot and I can't stop until I'm uncomfortably full, even when I try to tell myself to. I don't throw up or use laxatives, but the next day I force myself to go on long, punishing walks and restrict myself to just coffee and an apple to "balance the books."
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself? Are you very afraid of gaining weight even when others say your weight is normal?

It has a massive impact on how I feel about myself. Even when my wife tells me I look fine, I find myself pinching my stomach in the mirror and thinking I'm getting soft and useless. That single thought pretty much decides whether I have a good or bad day, regardless of what else I've accomplished.
How often do these binge-eating episodes and the next-day restriction or punishing walks happen—about how many times per week, and for how many months has this been going on?

This cycle of late-night eating and then punishing myself the next day happens about once or twice a week. It has been going on for about four months now, starting right around the time I transitioned to my reduced work schedule.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes with loss of control, followed by recurrent compensatory behaviors aimed at preventing weight gain (fasting/restriction and excessive exercise). Self-evaluation is markedly influenced by body shape and weight, and episodes occur 1–2 times per week for about 4 months. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.
